title: DO WHILE — F90 construct; condition evaluated BEFORE each iteration (no do-until)
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE FIND_FIRST_POSITIVE(A, N, IDX)
C     DO WHILE (cond) is F90+ and evaluates the condition BEFORE
C     each iteration -- like Java/C# 'while' (NOT 'do-while'). IDX
C     left at 0 if the array is empty.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      INTEGER N, IDX
      REAL    A(*)
      IDX = 1
      DO WHILE (IDX .LE. N .AND. A(IDX) .LE. 0.0)
         IDX = IDX + 1
      END DO
      IF (IDX .GT. N) IDX = 0
      END
notes: DO WHILE is straightforward but easy to miss. The trap here is the .AND. short-circuit: F77 .AND. does NOT guarantee short-circuit evaluation, so A(IDX) may be read with IDX > N. Java's && DOES short-circuit. A literal port to (idx <= n & a[idx] <= 0.0) — Java's & is non-short-circuit — re-introduces the bug.
